Notes.Text:
This update for trivy fixes the following issues:

- CVE-2026-19585: github.com/hashicorp/go-getter: path traversal during S3 and GCS directory downloads may allow files
  to be written outside the requested destination (bsc#1284829).
- CVE-2026-78669: golang.org/x/net/http2: excessive CPU consumption from repeated initial window changes (bsc#1285541).
- CVE-2026-97032: golang.org/x/net/http2: HTTP/2 server crash due to HPACK encoder race (bsc#1287329).

Vulnerabilities.Description: HashiCorp go-getter versions before 1.8.10 and go-getter/v2 versions before 2.2.5 are vulnerable to path traversal during S3 and GCS directory downloads, which may allow files to be written outside the requested destination. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-19585) is fixed in go-getter 1.8.10 and go-getter/v2 2.2.5.

A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption in the client or server by opening a large number of streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values.

HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when handling a SETTINGS frame containing SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious client can repeatedly send a request while changing the header table size to crash the server.
